hook: Someone has **grabbed my land.** What can I do?
hook_q: How do I get my land back?

slides.title: Act fast: the **6-month** suit.
slides.body: Dispossessed without your consent, and not by due process of law? You can sue to recover possession, even if they set up some other title in that suit.

slides.title: This quick suit has **limits.**
list: No appeal or review of the decision
You can still sue later on title

slides.title: Missed it? Sue **on title.**
slides.body: A person entitled to possession of specific immovable property, like land, can recover it by a civil suit under the Code of Civil Procedure. A suit for possession based on title generally has 12 years.
slides.ref: Specific Relief Act 1963 · Sec 5; Limitation Act 1963 · Art 65

timeline.text: Suit on earlier possession: **12 years** from the date of dispossession.
Suit on title: **12 years** from when their possession becomes adverse to you.
Your right to the property is **extinguished.**

slides.title: Trespass is **a crime.**
slides.body: Entering or staying on property in another's possession to commit an offence, or intimidate, insult or annoy, is criminal trespass: up to 3 months' jail, ₹5,000 fine, or both. In a home: up to 1 year.

slides.title: Tell the **police.**
slides.body: You can give information about the offence to the officer in charge of a police station, orally or by electronic communication.

sources: Specific Relief Act, 1963 (as amended by Act 18 of 2018) – Sections 5, 6
caption:
Someone has taken over your land? Here's what the law lets you do. 👇

1️⃣ Thrown out without consent and without due process? Sue to get possession back within 6 months of dispossession
2️⃣ That quick suit can't be filed against the Government, and there's no appeal, but you can still sue on title later
3️⃣ A suit for possession based on title generally has 12 years
4️⃣ Once the limitation period ends, your right to the property is extinguished, so don't wait
5️⃣ Criminal trespass is punishable with up to 3 months' jail, a ₹5,000 fine, or both (up to 1 year for a home)
6️⃣ You can give the information to the police station's officer in charge
⚠️ Check your State's laws too: Gujarat, for example, has a Land Grabbing (Prohibition) Act, 2020

Source: Specific Relief Act, 1963 (Sec 5, 6); Limitation Act, 1963 (Sec 27, Art 64, 65); Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Sec 329); BNSS, 2023 (Sec 173)
